candidate_rule_check.note: robustness check only; the pre-declared candidate is not re-selected
candidate_rule_check.rule: the encoder x head combination with the highest mean out-of-fold AUROC point estimate over the pre-declared S3 training seeds; ties resolved toward meanpool_logreg, then handcrafted; the candidate model is that combination's run with the first pre-declared seed

caveats: Development out-of-fold estimates on 35 development patients (45 slide bags); not test results. The test split is not read by this script.

Nothing is retrained: the exclusion removes the held-out predictions of the candidate patients, whose fold models may have trained on a near-duplicate partner. Fold models, thresholds and calibration are unchanged.

The candidates are an automated thumbnail-dHash screen with no human decision: they may be distinct material. The exclusion is a sensitivity bound for that question, not a finding that they are duplicates.
AUROC and AUPRC are threshold-free. Sensitivity / specificity deltas and McNemar use thresholds selected on the full OOF scores (Youden): tuning estimates (optimistic), flagged tuning_set.

The bootstrap uses the same seeds as s3 but a different patient set after exclusion, so the full and the restricted intervals come from different replicate streams; their difference is not a paired estimate.
Training-seed repeats measure optimisation variability on the same patients and folds; they are not additional independent patients.
Removing patients makes the intervals wider and the estimates noisier; with 31 patients CIs remain approximate.

Per-pair intervals are unadjusted for the several comparisons (4 per seed x 3 seeds, in two analyses): an interval that excludes 0 in one analysis is not a declared difference, and no winner is declared.
The candidate-rule check re-applies the s3 rule to the restricted numbers for robustness only; it never changes the pre-declared test candidate, which was fixed before any test access.

near_duplicates.rule: every patient of every near-duplicate candidate pair WITHOUT a human decision is excluded from the evaluation (both members, all of their development slides)

screen.source: dermpath.datasets._near_duplicates over the frozen manifest (the dataset audit's own screen) with the project's latest near-duplicate decisions

notice: RESEARCH USE ONLY. Not a medical device; nothing here is a diagnosis or a clinical performance claim. Labels are COBRA's report-derived imported reference labels (not expert reads in this workbench): metrics measure agreement with that reference. 'BCC absent' is not 'benign'.
